verbs.synopsis: boot a new session and print its id
verbs.usage:
usage: ks run [--image NAME] [--workspace PATH] [--budget TOKENS]

  --image NAME       guest image to boot (default "base"; e.g. counter, claude, aider)
  --workspace PATH   host path vendored into the guest workspace
  --budget TOKENS    per-session token budget enforced by ksgw (default 2000000)

Prints the new session id. Exceeding the budget pauses the session with a
checkpoint, never a silent kill.

verbs.synopsis: list sessions and their true state
verbs.usage:
usage: ks ps [--json]

  --json   machine-readable output

STATE is verified against the recorded VMM process at read time, not merely
reported from the last transition (BACKLOG #1). A session whose VMM is gone
reads "dead", whatever the database last wrote.

verbs.synopsis: attach to a session's tmux (humans attach, never own)
verbs.usage:
usage: ks attach SESSION

Attaches to tmux session "main" inside the guest. Detach with Ctrl-b d.

verbs.synopsis: freeze a session into content-addressed chunks (alias: save)
verbs.usage:
usage: ks checkpoint SESSION [--stop]

  --stop   leave the microVM stopped after the checkpoint

Publishing is crash-consistent: chunks, fsync, manifest to a temp name, fsync,
atomic rename. A checkpoint does not exist until its manifest has renamed.

usage: ks resume SESSION

Recreates the tap, restores the VMM from chunks, resyncs the guest clock, and
reconciles the guest and host ledgers before the specimen wakes.

verbs.synopsis: branch a checkpoint into divergent lineages
verbs.usage:
usage: ks fork SESSION [-n COUNT] [--steer FILE]

  -n COUNT       number of children (default 1)
  --steer FILE   per-branch steering text, injected by ksgw, never in the guest

Each child gets its own lineage id, its own writable disk, and its own egress
namespace, so identical guest IPs coexist.

verbs.synopsis: what a session cost, per call, replays excluded from spend

usage: ks meter SESSION [--json]

The RETRY column shows "replayed" for a call served from the store after an

verbs.synopsis: the full demo: an agent killed with its own daemon, then resumed
verbs.usage:
usage: ks demo [--task NAME] [--kill-at DURATION|manual] [--wait-for-kill]
            [--checkpoint-every DURATION] [--budget TOKENS] [--headless]
            [--report PATH] [--no-checkpoint]

  --task NAME              fixture task to vendor (default "fixture")
  --kill-at DURATION       kill this long after the specimen starts (default 3m).
                           Use "manual" to wait for a human instead.
  --wait-for-kill          arm, print the kill instruction, and block until a
                           human kills the VMM by hand. Same as --kill-at manual.
  --checkpoint-every DUR   checkpoint cadence (default 5m)
  --budget TOKENS          session token budget (default 400000)
  --headless               no tmux attach; log to stdout
  --report PATH            where to write the run report
  --no-checkpoint          SABOTAGE: disable checkpointing, so resume must fail

Needs a provider key in /etc/keepstate/ksgw.env (mode 600, root-owned) and
must run as root, because the guest key and the chunk store are root-only.

verbs.synopsis: reclaim rebuildable scratch from sessions with no live VMM
verbs.usage:
usage: ks gc [--yes] [--json]

  (default)  dry run: list what would be reclaimed and how many bytes
  --yes      actually delete
  --json     machine-readable output

gc deletes only what a resume can rebuild: per-session scratch and reassembled
per-generation state, and only for sessions with no live VMM. Chunks,
manifests, ledgers, and everything under preserved/ are ineligible by
construction (ADR-011). Every run that deletes writes a ledger event naming
what it removed and why it was rebuildable.

changelog.body:
KeepState v0.1.1 · the five wrap defects, fixed under the Patch Law

A patch release. No new claims: docs/claims.md is unchanged, every gate tag
still means what it meant, and nothing here promises anything v0.1.0-mvp did
not already prove.

THE PATCH LAW, recorded in CLAUDE.md before any code changed

  A bug is fixed when its BACKLOG reproduction command is run RED before the
  change and GREEN after it, and a permanent regression guard exists. Fix,
  reproduction, and guard land in the SAME commit. No silent fixes.

EACH ENTRY, ITS COMMIT, AND ITS GUARD

  #1  ks ps reported running for dead VMMs
      commit 389777c fix #1: ks ps reports verified liveness, not remembered intent
  #2  ks demo --help booted a demo
      commit 7e55ef5 fix #2: --help answered before any side effect, on every subcommand
  #3  no garbage collection
      commit 09166a9 fix #3: ks gc, per ADR-011 · deletes only what a resume can rebuild
  #4  no human-triggered kill
      commit d78706a fix #4: ks demo --kill-at manual waits for the human to pull the trigger
  #5  PRESERVED marker had an unexpanded date
      commit 51d7569 fix #5: PRESERVED marker records a real timestamp, and doctor checks that it does

  #1  guard: guards.sh #1 boots a session, proves it reads running, kills it,
      proves it reads dead, and requires the state.reconciled audit record.
  #2  guard: guards.sh #2 runs --help across all 17 verbs asserting usage,
      exit 0, and zero change in process and session counts; usage_test.go.
  #3  guard: guards.sh #3 builds a bench with a live session, a terminated
      one, and the preserved artifact, then requires the collected session to
      RESUME with its overlay rebuilt; doctor check 9 watches preserved/.
  #4  guard: guards.sh #4 asserts the demo is still blocked 20s after arming,
      then kills by hand and requires the resume.
  #5  guard: doctor check 8 rejects markers with unexpanded format verbs, no
      ruling, or no parseable timestamp; the shipped marker is a test case.

  Full suite: 29 guards, 0 failures.

MEASURED

  Reclaimed          session tree 82 G -> 15 G by ks gc (ADR-011)
  Demo downtime      19.0 s, re-rehearsed headless on the patched binaries
  Manual-kill demo   20.7 s, human kill detected and resumed
  Doctor             9/9 · the count is now derived, not hardcoded

REGRESSION SWEEP

  Green: gates 0, 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4, 5.
  Gates 2a, 2b, 3 and 5 first went RED and were green on re-run from a clean
  bench; the causes were the daemon restart race (BACKLOG #6), a client that
  did not retry while the gateway held the response, and one branch's steered
  call not landing in the window. None was a behavioral regression.

  Gate 6 was NOT re-run, by explicit determination: its claim rests on ksd's
  checkpoint path, internal/soak/ has a zero-line diff since v0.1.0-mvp, and
  the only new functions in manager.go are the two liveness helpers.

  Gate 7 is RED and BLOCKED on a human ruling. Neither failure is a v0.1.1
  regression, and BLOCKED.md carries the options and a recommendation:
    B1 pins a baseline from ADR-010 and demands an empty core diff, so ANY
       patch fails it permanently · a ratchet nobody intended.
    B6 catches a real defect introduced during the v0.1.0 release wrap: the
       compatibility matrix is a table in the anti-claims section and its
       header row cites no tag. claims.md was deliberately NOT edited  · 
       B6 audits that file, and editing it to pass the audit during the same
       session that runs the audit is what rule 7 forbids.

FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED (scope law: the five entries, nothing else)

  #6  ksd exits instead of waiting when its port is briefly still held.
  #7  internal/ksd/netid.go is not gofmt-clean (drift from Phase 5).
  #8  gate 7's B1 baseline pin (see BLOCKED.md).
  #9  claims.md fails its own B6 check (see BLOCKED.md).
  #10 ksgw writes the meter into a table it no longer has, silently. A whole
      demo served ten calls and the billing ledger recorded none, with zero
      errors logged. The most serious entry on the list: the meter is the
      evidence behind the billed-at-most-once claim.

FOUNDER DECISION RECORDED

  The core stays unlicensed, all rights reserved. The han protocol is
  extracted to its own repository under Apache-2.0 the day the first design
  partner is live · an event, not a date, because a protocol with no
  implementers is documentation with a patent grant attached. Reasoning in
  BACKLOG.md.

KeepState v0.1.0-mvp · the durable agent session cloud

An MVP that runs AI agents inside Firecracker microVMs and gives them five
verbs: run, checkpoint, fork, resume, replay. A live agent is killed mid-task
 ·  the microVM and the daemon supervising it · and is working again seconds
later, same session, same memory, mid-sentence.

Frozen at nine green gates. The standing invariant is that no claim outlives
its gate and no claim precedes one; docs/claims.md is the promise surface and
gate 7 machine-checks that every row in it cites a tag that exists.

THE NINE GATES

  gate-0-green   the bench can host KVM microVMs
  gate-1-green   a microVM died mid-count and woke up mid-sentence
  gate-2a-green  ksd carries sessions across kill-and-resume, twice in a row
  gate-2b-green  checkpoints are portable, forkable, crash-consistent objects
  gate-3-green   a real specimen was frozen mid-thought and resumed, billed once
  gate-4-green   one command, an agent killed with its own daemon, back at work in 25 seconds
  gate-5-green   three branches, one checkpoint, three histories that differ only by their steer
  gate-6-green   durability measured as a rate, 25/25 with a Wilson interval that admits what 25 trials can carry
  gate-7-green   a second agent and a second machine, with zero core changes

MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED

  Resume success rate      25/25 fresh kill-and-resume cycles;
                           Wilson 95% CI [86.7%, 100.0%]   (gate-6-green)
  Downtime                 19.8 s this release's rehearsal; 25.2 s in gate 4;
                           13.7 s for an agent session in gate 7.
                           Chunk reassembly dominates; the VMM needs ~4 ms.
  Storage                  82 checkpoints in 4,233 MiB against 80,952 MiB
                           naive · 19.1x dedup            (gate-6-green)
  Daemon memory            7-hour soak, 82 checkpoints: ksd +0 MiB,
                           ksgw +0 MiB peak RSS growth    (gate-6-green)
  Core changes for agent 2 zero · git diff over cmd/ and internal/ empty
                           since the gate's pinned baseline (gate-7-green)

REPRODUCIBLE EVIDENCE

  Preserved artifact soak-20712ae21ba9, held under the Phase 6 preservation
  ruling of 2026-07-30 at /var/lib/keepstate/preserved/ on the build bench:
  587 chunks, 741 MiB, self-contained (manifest plus its own chunks).
  Verified at release: 587 of 587 manifest-referenced chunks present, none
  missing; spot-checked chunks hash to their own names, since a chunk's name
  is the sha256 of its uncompressed bytes. This is the ~14.5-hour-old
  checkpoint that gate 6 woke in 14.3 s · a checkpoint does not go stale.

  QUICKSTART.md is executable evidence: gate 7 extracts its commands
  mechanically and runs them on a machine that has never built KeepState.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED

  One provider path, one host, aarch64 only, resume in seconds rather than
  sub-second, and a client-retry story that differs per agent · for aider the
  gateway held the interrupted response 4 of 4 times while the client walked
  back through 3 of 4. See docs/limitations.md, where every limit cites the
  measurement or names the gate that does not exist, and BACKLOG.md, which
  records five defects found during the release wrap and deliberately not
  fixed under a docs-only scope law.

  No LICENSE file: all rights reserved by default, pending a founder decision
  between an open protocol and a hosted core, recorded in BACKLOG.md.

START HERE

  README.md         what this is, and the nine tags
  QUICKSTART.md     clean clone to your first kill-and-resume, ~20 minutes
  OPERATOR.md       cold start to healthy bench in literal commands
  DEMO_SCRIPT.md    the on-camera run, beat by beat
  docs/claims.md    every claim and the gate tag that proves it

gate-7 green: a second agent and a second machine, with zero core changes

aider 0.86.2 frozen mid-call, killed, resumed. The entire agent-specific
surface is one exported alias inside the image; git diff --stat over cmd and
internal since the gate's pinned baseline is empty. A stranger's machine
reached RAM continuity from a clean clone using only QUICKSTART.md's own
commands.

Two findings, both about the court rather than the product. The client's
return is not ours to promise: across four runs the gateway held the response
4 of 4 while the client came back 3 of 4, so the promise split with the
behavior. And assert the fact, not the residue: an assertion that checked for
a file ADR-006 consumes by design could only pass when the client never
returned, punishing the system for succeeding.

Sabotage green: seq stamping disabled collapsed the gap to 0 and the
reconciliation assertion failed exactly as it should.

gate-6 green: durability measured as a rate, 25/25 with a Wilson interval that admits what 25 trials can carry

Three findings, none in the core claim. A connection leak that killed any
session past its ninth checkpoint and that 25 kill-cycles structurally could
not see · the soak exists because kill-cycles reset the very counters that
long-lived sessions accumulate. A preservation breach where our own cleanup
destroyed the artifact a ruling had protected. And a gate that could not read
its own evidence while the system was healthy: six false alarms and one false
comfort from a single parser defect.

The fix for the third is a mechanism, not a promise: ks ledger, production Go
code sharing the writers' types, now the only path a gate may read evidence
through.

82/82 scheduled checkpoints, one witness nonce strictly monotonic, zero
cadence gaps, 19.1x dedup, RSS peak growth +0 MiB on both daemons. A
14.5-hour-old checkpoint woken live in 14.3 s reading COUNT=63 while its
living twin had reached 4841.

gate-5 green: three branches, one checkpoint, three histories that differ only by their steer

The MVP build plan is complete · gates 0, 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4 and 5 all green.

Phase 5 solved the deferred child-egress dragon the honest way: a forked
guest keeps the parent's addressing and never learns it was cloned, while
per-child network namespaces let identical guest IPs coexist and reach the
gateway independently. Steering lives only in ksgw, injected into a branch's
next call and recorded with both pre- and post-steer body hashes · which is
how the gate proved three siblings differed by their steering and by nothing
else: base sha256 identical on all three, steered bodies all distinct.

The gate earned its keep. It caught an attribution bug that billed every
forked child's work to its parent, and two more besides. All three were
fixed and disclosed before the gate re-ran.

gate-4 green: one command, an agent killed with its own daemon, back at work in 25 seconds

The demo the company was built to give. `ks demo --task fixture --kill-at 3m
--headless` boots a real Claude Code specimen on a vendored four-bug repo,
checkpoints it, then hard-kills BOTH the microVM and ksd itself · the daemon
that supervises it · restarts the daemon, and resumes. Measured downtime:
25.2 seconds, of which Firecracker's own snapshot/load was 4 milliseconds.
The specimen came back and fixed all four bugs.

29,871 tokens were not re-purchased: work already paid for when the kill
landed, served from the gateway's store instead of bought twice. That number
is MEASURED. The dollar figure beside it is labeled ESTIMATED, because the
rates are an assumption and the tokens are not.

Sabotage green: with checkpointing disabled the same kill is unsurvivable.
gate-3 green: a real specimen was frozen mid-thought and resumed, billed once
gate-2b green: checkpoints are portable, forkable, crash-consistent objects
gate-2a green: ksd carries sessions across kill-and-resume, twice in a row
gate-1 green: a microVM died mid-count and woke up mid-sentence
